summary: Independent first pass on uncommitted decision-workspace implementation above HEAD 833c0eb424e078d06bc01ad235efb5aa97be75db. Two medium findings reproduced: validity duration is absent from the evidence approval display, and missing requirement-state rows evade batch overlap detection. The three focused SQLite suites pass 25 tests. No additional material findings identified in the attention, metrics, tenancy, or transactional rollback scope examined.

Inspected all listed core/server proposal-review and attention sources, proposal sections of VisuaService/app routes, workspaceSummary in views.ts, and frontend Proposals.tsx/AgentsPage.tsx, OverviewMetrics.tsx/AttentionQueue.tsx/HomePage.tsx, queries and event invalidation. Source hashes are in .check/independent-review/inspected-source.json; every ten-path server/core/test digest in independent-review-source.json matched at first-pass completion.

Traced all ten proposal types into existing service mutations, canonical snapshot inputs, generated field projection, persisted connector observations, inline/file evidence review boundaries, UTC-day token invalidation, existing/new targets, fixed batch sets, overlap handling, single-item and decision-audit failure behavior.

Inspected Store.atomic/transaction/afterCommit and VisuaService.mutate/emit/log paths: nested savepoint callback ownership, rollback behavior, workspace locks and audit revision behavior; checked workspaceAccess capability floor and explicit work.approve guards, foreign proposal/source/run ownership checks, and corresponding API/auth tests.

Inspected attention/test fixtures and scoring/status/graph dependencies for all enabled frameworks, disabled/withdrawn/user-excluded nodes, statutory dates, assessable versus group links, latest-per-connector/check/requirement results, accepted current review and artifact freshness, alternative valid evidence, owner identity, due-day ordering, filtering before presentation limits, and fresh metric reads.

This includes transactional no-side-effect preview, token staleness, tenant/capability protection, fixed batch membership, existing-row overlaps, partial storage/audit failures, authoritative observations, file review blocking, group exclusions and current expiry metrics.

findings.mechanism: Trigger: review a narrative create-evidence proposal with validDays specified. Projection omits collectedAt and validUntil from both the new evidence record and review scope as generated timestamps, and the only duration explanation says the validity period begins at approval. PreviewContent renders changes/sources/questions but never the original payload.validDays. Therefore a one-day acceptance and a 730-day acceptance are visually indistinguishable, despite that duration controlling valid evidence coverage after approval.
findings.evidence: Isolated repro-output.txt VALIDITY_DURATION contains validDays=1 and validDays=730 records with identical changes, sources and questions. Both list validUntil as a generated field but contain no duration. The actual mutation uses payload.validDays to set validUntil at apps/server/src/services/visua.ts:1990. The exposed proposal payload still contains the value, so this finding concerns the human review display rather than missing token binding.
findings.recommendation: Expose the stable validity rule in the authoritative preview and render it, for example collected at approval and expires 730 days after approval (or no expiration). Keep exact runtime timestamps identified as generated. Add a regression proving 1, 730, and omitted validDays produce distinct, explicit review semantics.

findings.mechanism: Trigger: two batch proposals target the same known requirement before its state row exists, such as a newly ingested unit in an existing workspace. updateState explicitly supports this state at visua.ts:917-928. changesBetween omits entityId whenever current is absent, even though the requirement nodeId is already fixed. Batch overlap detection requires entityId, so both changes pass as independent and execute sequentially; the second overwrites or acts on the first instead of applying the independently reviewed before-state.
findings.evidence: The isolated reproduction deleted only disposable fixture state rows, created two set-level proposals for nist-csf-2.0:PR.AA-01 with current=1 and current=4, and previewed/approved their exact batch token. MISSING_STATE_BATCH output shows both previews with current:null and no entityId, conflicts:[], result applied:2/skipped:0, and final current:4. No persisted production/shared database was touched. Source confirms initialization occurs during workspace creation/framework enable, while updateState provides the missing-row fallback.
findings.recommendation: Retain the canonical nodeId as entityId for requirement changes even when the state row is newly created, or derive overlap targets from proposal operation identities independently of before-row existence. Verify both overlapping proposals remain pending/skipped and no target state is created by batch approval.

limitations: This report preserves the original first-pass findings and source state. The lead accepted both findings and assigned corrections after the first pass; those later corrections are not covered by this original report and need a focused recheck.

Runtime checks were isolated SQLite only. PostgreSQL concurrency, a full suite, builds, browser suites, visual rendering, and large-workspace performance were not executed by this reviewer; those checks remain with the lead. Frontend snapshot/display conclusions come from source tracing rather than a browser run.

The missing-state reproduction used a controlled deletion in a disposable in-memory fixture to exercise the supported fallback; it does not establish that currently deployed workspace rows are missing. Group-only checks were inspected but stock connector outputs reviewed use assessable requirement links.
